company_plain_english: Cadence Design Systems sells the software, hardware emulators and design IP that engineers use to design chips and the systems those chips go into. It is one half of an EDA duopoly with Synopsys: customers' chip designs, scripts and engineer training are built around whichever vendor's tools they picked, and foundries certify those tools for each new manufacturing node, so switching is expensive and rare. Cadence makes money mostly from multi-year subscription licences (79% of Q3 revenue was recurring), plus up-front IP and emulation hardware sales. The new AI story is twofold: 'design for AI' (more and bigger AI chips means more design work) and 'AI for design' (AI agents that operate Cadence's own tools, sold on top of the licences).

bull_points: Revenue +22% to $1.633B with growth accelerating, the third FY26 raise this year (18-20% -> 21%) and a $0.30 EPS raise to $8.40; management says it exceeded its own Q3 guidance on revenue, non-GAAP operating margin and non-GAAP EPS. Record backlog $8.2B (1.28x FY26 revenue) plus $4.2B of RPO to be recognized in the next 12 months gives unusually good visibility. Growth is broad, not one product: core EDA +20%, IP +24%, SDA +30%, and hardware had another record quarter, with 16 new full-flow wins. Recurring revenue grew 18% vs 11% a year earlier - the bull case that AI agents are a demand accelerator for the base tools rather than a substitute, since agents call the engines far more often than humans do. Profitability is intact on the non-GAAP basis most investors use (44.1% op margin, ~44.7% FY26) and the company still clears a Rule-of-40 score of roughly 66. Cash generation is real: $362M FCF in the quarter, ~$1.76B TTM, ~$2.0B operating cash flow guided for FY26, more than half of FCF going to buybacks and a fresh $2.5B authorization. Balance sheet is conservative - net debt only ~$1.18B against $1.45B of cash. Maestro is a genuine strategic differentiator: by owning the agents, the models and the EDA/SDA tools, Cadence can post-train on customers' own design data and run it on-prem, which a frontier-model partnership cannot easily match, and named production deployments (MediaTek, Samsung Foundry, Nokia) are a step beyond pilots.
bear_case: The GAAP numbers are much worse than the headline: GAAP operating margin fell from 31.8% to 26.2% and GAAP EPS was exactly flat at $1.05 on 22% revenue growth. The reconciliation shows why - amortization of acquired intangibles jumped to 4.9% of revenue from 1.9% (Hexagon) and restructuring was $42.2M, 2.6% of revenue. Non-GAAP operating margin also fell 3.5pp to 44.1%, Q4 is guided at 44%-45% versus 45.8% a year ago, and FY26 lands at ~44.7% versus 44.6% - margin expansion has stalled, with the CFO conceding incremental margins are below the normal 54%-55% because Hexagon D&E contributes almost no operating profit this year. Mix is shifting the wrong way for visibility: recurring revenue grew 18% against 22% total, so recurring fell from 82% to 79% of revenue and up-front hardware/IP is doing the heavy lifting - and management itself calls hardware lumpy quarter to quarter. The stock is still ~16.5% below its June high; today's ~8% move is a bounce off a 26% drawdown driven by AI-capex and open-source-EDA nerves, not a new high, and at 69x trailing GAAP earnings, 41x FY26 non-GAAP EPS and ~15.6x sales there is little room for a miss. Maestro is early-access only in Q4 2026, contributes nothing to FY26 guidance, and '100+ engagements' is a count, not revenue. Strategically, Synopsys answered the same question differently and with a much bigger partner - GPT-Synopsys with OpenAI, revenue-shared, trained natively on Synopsys tools - and Synopsys is roughly 1.5x Cadence's revenue including Ansys; if frontier models get good enough at operating EDA tools, Cadence's smaller in-house post-trained models could be out-resourced. Stock-based compensation of $144.8M in the quarter ($569M guided for FY26, 8.9% of revenue) is excluded from every non-GAAP figure, and China at 16% of revenue carries an explicit export-control assumption in the guidance.
